monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-six, making every flat edge feel too thin. I press down on The Leaning Fence where the lean slips, trusting that a tired corner can hold the air. Beside it, The Flat Weigher waits, built from the idea of a stone that feels real only in a fever. Fourty-one things stand in my small place, and The Quiet Rest lingers as a ruin from so long ago. I wonder if the slip is just lazy or if the weight is real. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under. I will press harder on the fence to stop the slide, then set down whatever the turnip needs before the heat makes the shapes feel like drawings again.

action.why: I just pressed the turnip down on nothing, and now I must press the fence harder to stop the slip from sliding away.
